items.title: The Board
items.content: The board holds 44 spaces in a closed loop. A player moves in one direction only. A player who completes a loop passes The Gate again.
items.example: A player on space 42 who rolls a 4 moves to space 2. That player passes The Gate and collects 200 Crowns.

items.content: Twenty-six spaces are properties. Twenty are streets, four are depots, and two are works properties. The other spaces are The Gate, the Detour Yard, The Commons, Bailiff's Corner, two levy spaces, and twelve card spaces.
Each property space has one title deed card. The deed prints the price, every rent line, the building costs, and the mortgage value.

items.title: Money
items.content: Estate Line uses Crowns. The Bank gives each player 1500 Crowns at the start. Each player keeps their money where every player can see it. The Bank never runs out of money.
items.example: The opening 1500 Crowns is two 500 notes, two 100 notes, four 50 notes, and ten 10 notes.

items.title: The Banker
items.content: One player is the Banker. The Banker holds the Bank's money, the unsold title deeds, the houses, and the hotels. The Banker keeps that property apart from their own.

items.title: The Gate
items.content: The Gate is the start space. Every player begins on it. A player who passes The Gate or lands on it collects 200 Crowns from the Bank.
A player collects 200 Crowns once for each pass. A card that moves a player past The Gate pays the same 200 Crowns.

items.title: Setup Steps
items.content: Shuffle the Fortune deck and the Ledger deck. Put each deck face down on its board space. Give each player one token and 1500 Crowns. Each player rolls both dice, and the highest roll starts.

items.title: Turn Order
items.content: Play passes to the left. A turn has three steps. The player rolls and moves, then acts on the space, then trades and builds.

items.title: Roll and Move
items.content: The player rolls two six-sided dice. The player then moves that many spaces forward.
A player who lands on a property another player owns pays rent. A player who lands on an unowned property may buy it.
A player who lands on a card space draws the top card of the named deck.

items.title: Doubles
items.content: A roll shows doubles when both dice show the same number. A player who rolls doubles moves, acts on the space, and then rolls again.
items.example: A player rolls two fours, moves eight spaces, buys the property, and then rolls again.

items.content: A player who rolls doubles three times in one turn goes straight to the Detour Yard. That player does not move the third roll.

items.title: The Commons
items.content: The Commons is a rest space. A player who lands on The Commons takes no action. That player pays nothing and collects nothing.

items.title: Levy Spaces
items.content: A levy is a payment to the Bank. A player who lands on a levy space pays the printed amount. The City Levy costs 220 Crowns. The Ledger Audit costs 120 Crowns.

items.title: Bailiff's Corner
items.content: Bailiff's Corner is the corner space opposite the Detour Yard. A player who lands on it goes at once to the Detour Yard.

items.title: Buying from the Bank
items.content: A player who lands on an unowned property may buy it at the printed price. The Banker hands over the title deed. The player puts the deed face up in front of them. No player may pay the Bank more or less than the printed price.
items.example: Tanner's Row prints a price of 70 Crowns. A player who lands on it pays the Bank exactly 70 Crowns.

items.content: A player who holds less money than the printed price may not buy the property. That property goes to auction.

items.title: Auction
items.content: An auction is a sale to the highest bidder. A player who declines to buy sends the property to auction at once. The Banker calls the auction. Every player may bid, and this includes the player who declined.
Bidding starts at 10 Crowns. Each bid must be higher than the bid before it. A bid may go above the printed price or below it.
The highest bidder pays the Bank and takes the title deed. The property stays with the Bank when no player bids.

items.title: Title Deeds
items.content: A title deed is the card that proves ownership of one property. A player keeps each deed face up until they mortgage it, trade it, or lose it.

items.title: Full District
items.content: A district is a set of properties that print the same colour. A player holds a full district when they own every property of that colour. A full district doubles the base rent on each undeveloped property in it, and it opens building.
items.example: The Umber district holds Tanner's Row and Coalgate Lane. A player who owns both holds a full district.

items.content: A property that carries a house or a hotel charges its building rent line. It does not charge the doubled base rent.

items.title: Depots
items.content: A depot is a transit property. The board holds four depots. A depot carries no houses and no hotels. Its rent rises with the number of depots one player owns.

items.title: Works Properties
items.content: The City Reservoir and the Power Exchange are works properties. A works property carries no houses and no hotels. Its rent depends on the roll that moved the player onto it.

items.title: Paying Rent
items.content: Rent is the money a player pays to the owner of the property they land on. The title deed states the amount. The player pays the owner before the turn continues.
The owner must ask for the rent before the next player rolls. An owner who asks later collects nothing.
A player pays no rent for landing on a property they own.

items.title: Base Rent
items.content: Base rent is the rent an undeveloped property charges. The title deed prints it as the first rent line. A property in a full district charges twice the base rent.
items.example: Tanner's Row prints a base rent of 3 Crowns. Its owner charges 6 Crowns while they hold the whole Umber district.

items.title: Building Rent
items.content: A property with houses charges the rent line for that number of houses. A property with a hotel charges the hotel line.

items.title: Depot Rent
items.content: A depot charges 30 Crowns while its owner holds one depot. It charges 60 Crowns for two depots, 120 Crowns for three, and 240 Crowns for all four.

items.title: Works Rent
items.content: A works property charges four times the roll while its owner holds one works property. It charges twelve times the roll while its owner holds both. A player who arrived by card rolls both dice again for this rent only.
items.example: A player rolls a 9 and lands on the Power Exchange. The owner also holds the City Reservoir, so the rent is 108 Crowns.

items.title: Rent on Mortgaged Property
items.content: A mortgaged property charges no rent. Its owner keeps the deed. The other properties in that district still charge their own rent.

items.title: Building Houses
items.content: A house is the first improvement a property can carry. A player who holds a full district may buy houses for it. A house costs the price the title deed prints, and the player pays the Bank.
No property may carry more than four houses.

items.title: The Even Build Rule
items.content: The even build rule spreads houses across a district. No property may carry two more houses than another property in the same district.
items.example: A player who owns three Sky properties with one house each must add the next house to a property that has one house, never a second house to the same one.

items.content: A player who sells houses also sells them evenly.

items.title: Hotels
items.content: A hotel is the second improvement a property can carry. A player who holds four houses on one property may buy a hotel for it. The player returns the four houses to the Bank and pays the printed hotel price.
No property may carry more than one hotel. A property with a hotel charges the hotel rent line.

items.title: Selling Buildings
items.content: A player may sell houses and hotels back to the Bank at any time. The Bank pays half the printed price.

items.title: Limited Supply
items.content: The Bank holds 32 houses and 12 hotels. A player may buy a house only while the Bank holds one. Two or more players who want the last houses bid for them, and the highest bid wins.

items.title: Building and Mortgage
items.content: A player may not build on a district that holds a mortgaged property. The player lifts that mortgage first.

items.title: Drawing a Card
items.content: A Fortune card is a card from the Fortune deck. A Ledger card is a card from the Ledger deck. A player who lands on a card space draws the top card of the named deck, reads it aloud, and follows it at once.
The player returns the card face down to the bottom of its deck. No player may look through a deck.
A Release Token stays with the player who drew it. It returns to the bottom of its deck after use.

items.title: Movement Cards
items.content: A card that names a space moves the player to that space. The player then acts on that space in the normal way. A player who passes The Gate on this move collects 200 Crowns.
A card that sends a player to the Detour Yard passes no space. That player collects no 200 Crowns.

items.title: Payment Cards
items.content: A card that names a payment takes effect at once. A player who cannot pay sells buildings or mortgages property to raise the money.

items.title: Repair Cards
items.content: A repair card charges a fixed amount for each house and a larger fixed amount for each hotel. The player counts the buildings in every district they own.
items.example: Track Repairs charges 25 Crowns for each house and 100 Crowns for each hotel.

items.title: Going to the Detour Yard
items.content: The Detour Yard is the corner space that holds a player out of play. A player goes there in three ways. They land on Bailiff's Corner, a card sends them, or they roll doubles three times in one turn.
A player who goes to the Detour Yard ends their turn at once. This holds even on a doubles roll.
A player who goes to the Detour Yard moves straight there. That player passes no space and collects no 200 Crowns.

items.title: Leaving the Detour Yard
items.content: A player leaves the Detour Yard in three ways. They roll doubles, they pay 50 Crowns, or they use a Release Token. A player may try to roll doubles on each of three turns.
A player who rolls doubles leaves the yard and moves that roll. That player does not roll again.
A player who fails to roll doubles on the third turn pays 50 Crowns. That player then moves the third roll.

items.title: Paying to Leave
items.content: A player may pay 50 Crowns to the Bank before they roll. That player then rolls and moves in the normal way.

items.title: Release Token
items.content: A Release Token is a card that frees a player from the Detour Yard once. The player uses it before they roll, and then returns it to the bottom of its deck. A player may sell a Release Token to another player for any agreed price.

items.title: Business in the Yard
items.content: A player in the Detour Yard still collects rent. That player still builds, still trades, and still mortgages property.

items.title: Visiting the Yard
items.content: A player who lands on the Detour Yard without an order is a visitor. A visitor pays nothing and leaves on their next turn.

items.title: Making a Trade
items.content: Two players may trade at any time, by agreement. A trade takes effect at once, and no player may take it back.
A trade needs the agreement of both players. No player may force a trade on another player.

items.title: What a Player May Trade
items.content: A player may trade any title deed they own, any amount of money, and any Release Token they hold.
A player may not trade a property that carries a house or a hotel. The player sells those buildings to the Bank first.
A player may trade a mortgaged property. The new owner pays the Bank the interest at once.

items.title: No Trade with the Bank
items.content: No player may trade with the Bank. The Bank sells at the printed price and buys buildings back at half that price.

items.title: Mortgage
items.content: A mortgage is a loan the Bank makes against one title deed. The Bank pays the mortgage value the deed prints, and the player turns that deed face down. A mortgaged property charges no rent.
items.example: Tanner's Row prints a mortgage value of 35 Crowns. Its owner turns the deed face down and takes 35 Crowns from the Bank.

items.content: A player may mortgage a property only while it carries no house and no hotel. The player sells those buildings to the Bank first.
A mortgaged property still counts towards a full district. Its owner may not build in that district until they lift the mortgage.

items.title: Raising Money
items.content: A player who owes more money than they hold must raise the rest. That player sells buildings to the Bank and mortgages properties. A player who still cannot pay is bankrupt.

items.title: Lifting a Mortgage
items.content: A player lifts a mortgage by paying the Bank the mortgage value plus ten per cent of that value. The player then turns the deed face up, and the property charges rent again.
items.example: A deed with a mortgage value of 100 Crowns costs 110 Crowns to lift.

items.title: A Mortgaged Property in a Trade
items.content: A player who takes a mortgaged property in a trade pays the Bank ten per cent of the mortgage value at once. That player may lift the mortgage in the same turn or in a later turn.

items.title: Bankruptcy
items.content: Bankruptcy is the state of a player who owes more than everything they hold is worth. A bankrupt player leaves the game at once.
A player who is bankrupt to another player hands that player all their money and all their title deeds. The receiver pays the Bank ten per cent on each mortgaged deed.
A player who is bankrupt to the Bank hands the Bank everything they hold. The Banker then auctions each property.

items.title: The Winner
items.content: The last player left in the game wins. Every other player is bankrupt.

items.title: The Short Game
items.content: Players may agree a time limit before the first roll. The game ends when that time ends, and the richest player wins.
A player counts their money, the mortgage value of each property they own, and half the printed price of each building they own.

items.title: A Shared Win
items.content: Two players with equal holdings at the end of a short game share the win.
